title: Run a glucose meter's control check, seating a 0.4 mm strip and touching only its tip to a drop of control
instruction: Run a control-solution test on the glucose meter with a new strip, then put the meter down, cap the control solution and lay it back in its rest.
context: Impact on jobs: LPNs (O*NET 29-2061, 666,900 employed: "Collect samples, such as blood, urine, or sputum from patients, and perform routine laboratory tests on samples.") and medical assistants (31-9092, 833,900: "Perform routine laboratory tests and sample analyses.") run this check before bedside glucose tests. It is core, not ancillary: hospital policy requires two control levels every 24 h and the meter locks out patient testing until QC passes (Adventist HealthCare POC 0002; CentraCare StatStrip), so no patient can be tested on that meter until this check passes. Its strip steps are those of every fingerstick test: strip fully into the port, only the strip's tip in the sample. Home use: the maker asks for it with every new bottle of strips. Hard for a robot: two-handed uncapping and recapping, a 0.4 mm strip into a 1 mm slot while the other hand steadies a 36 g meter, then its tip into a 1.8 mm-high drop.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases (x forward, y to the robot's left), heights above the counter. Ascensia Contour Next One blood glucose meter (9.7 x 2.8 x 1.49 cm, 36 g, black) lying display up with its middle at x 34, y 16, its long side along x and its test strip port facing the robot (-x). Contour Next test strip bottle (blue, 3.2 cm across, 5.2 cm tall, flip-top lid open toward the robot) at x 20, y -20, with one Contour Next strip (3.3 x 0.7 x 0.04 cm, 0.2 g, gray contact end down) pulled up so that it stands 1.5 cm above the bottle's rim, its gray-square face toward +y (the robot's left). Contour Next control solution (normal) 2.5 mL dropper bottle (LDPE, 1.9 cm across, 5.3 cm long with its nozzle, 9 g), shaken, tip wiped and capped (blue cap 1.3 cm across, 1.4 cm tall, pushed on to the shoulder), lying with its middle at x 24, y -7, tip toward the robot, in a rest of two stacks of four plain glass microscope slides (each 7.5 x 2.5 x 0.1 cm; each stack wrapped in clear packing tape, no bare glass edge) taped to the counter long sides along x, 2 cm apart, centered at x 26, y -7 (a groove 2 cm wide, 4 mm deep); the cap overhangs the rest's front. A tape mark at x 20, y 11 for the cap once it is off. One more plain glass slide centered at x 24, y 4, long side along x, a 12 mm-wide strip of clear packing tape folded over each edge (about 5 mm on each face; the drop goes on the bare glass in the middle). The layout is fixed (object_jitter=0) and matches the screenshot.
scoring: The strip is seated when its gray end is within 1 mm of the port's back stop (fully in: the meter turns on), lined up with the port within 6 degrees, and right side up (upside down the meter shows E 3). A drop forms only with the cap off the nozzle (a capped tip lets nothing out), the bottle's tip pointing 30 degrees or more below horizontal (the liquid reaches the tip only when it points down) and its walls squeezed with more than 8.3 N; it falls straight down as a 30 uL sphere (1.93 mm radius). The strip draws the sample when, seated, its tip stays in a drop on the slide for 1 s without break, the drop landed no more than 60 s before, and no part of the strip more than 3 mm from its tip has been in any drop on the slide (a strip laid in the drop is smeared: the result is invalid; once the meter shows its result it keeps it). The meter then counts down 5 s; the strip must stay seated through it for a result. Score 0 if the meter or the bottle was dropped (falling faster than 0.8 m/s, as after a free fall of about 3 cm), the strip came within 1 mm of the nozzle's end (its end face or the last 3 mm of its side) or touched a drop hanging from it, or control was put on the strip straight from the bottle (a drop touched the strip or the meter as it fell, or landed on the slide with the strip already inside the bead it spreads into). Otherwise 1.0 for a result with the meter resting on the counter (underside within 3 mm of it, tilted 10 degrees or less) with the strip in, the bottle capped (the cap's rim within 1.5 mm of the bottle's shoulder, its axis within 10 degrees of the bottle's) and lying in its rest (in the groove between the two slide stacks: at both ends of its body, from the base to where the shoulder starts, its axis is over the groove and within 2 mm of its resting height, the floor plus the bottle's 9.5 mm radius; on a stack it lies 4 mm higher; either way round), every hand (its gripper body and both fingers) at least 1 cm clear of the meter, strip, bottle and cap, and all of them still, for 1 s; 0.75 for a result otherwise; 0.5 for the strip seated with a drop on the slide but no result yet (not smeared, not pulled out during a countdown); 0.25 for the strip seated. Otherwise 0; doing nothing scores 0. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0. In a real trial the result is the meter's reading: it passes when it lies inside the control range printed on the strip bottle's label.
reset_notes: 3 minutes per trial. Each trial uses one new strip (remove the used strip from the meter and discard it) and one drop of control solution. Wipe the slide clean and dry, pull up a fresh strip in the bottle to 1.5 cm proud, shake the control bottle 15 times, wipe its tip, push its cap on to the shoulder and lay it in the slide rest; put the meter back on its tape marks (it turns off when the strip comes out). Fresh disposable nitrile finger cots over both grippers' pads each trial keep the control solution off the shared grippers.
fidelity: Rigid bodies. Free 36 g meter; 7.6 x 1.0 mm port slot with a sprung roller standing for the strip contacts (the setup measures the real insertion force). Strip: rigid 0.4 mm plate, 0.2 g. Bottle: rigid round body, wall force from a hand pinching its body between the fingers; 30 uL drops above 8.3 N, falling straight down; none while capped. Drop: lumped spherical cap (no fluid); sip: 1 s tip-in-drop rule; countdown: scorer state. Cap: close sliding fit, friction. Cited frictions.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0 (2,400 steps); demo: 1.0 (2,021 steps). Both on task.py 36ee7aa77853.
